sections.h2: Why Round Rock's location draws buyers
sections.html:
Round Rock sits on Interstate 35 in south central Williamson County, roughly sixteen miles north of downtown Austin. Housing demand follows Austin's growth and Dell Technologies, which has its headquarters here. Expect buyers who commute toward Austin, work for technology employers, or want a house close to Old Settlers Park, the 570-acre park the city built with sales tax revenue.

Dell is the city's largest employer, and the city says the sales tax revenue from Dell sales has helped reduce property taxes for decades. A large employer base supports steady buyer interest, but your price still depends on your street, school zone and condition. Compare recent nearby sales rather than city-wide claims.

Old Town is a small cluster of restored limestone buildings now surrounded by the rest of the city. It matters if your house sits in a historic overlay area, because alterations to a structure or site with Historic Overlay Zoning need a Certificate of Appropriateness before a building permit. That includes fences and accessory structures.

Preservation staff can be reached through the Planning and Development Services desk at 512-218-5428. If you are selling an older home, ask whether the overlay applies before promising a buyer an addition or a new fence.

sections.h2: Building rules that can come up in a sale
sections.html:
Selling needs no permit, yet loose ends from past work can slow a contract. The city requires a permit to build, alter, repair or demolish, and for work on electrical, gas, mechanical or plumbing systems.

  • The city runs a one-permit system, so related electrical, plumbing and mechanical work goes on one permit, and all contractors must be named on it.
  • A permit becomes invalid if authorized work does not start within six months.
  • Contractors and subcontractors must register, with no registration or annual fee.
  • Sheds under 200 square feet and 15 feet tall still need a permit as accessory structures.

Carports, pergolas, pools and similar structures are allowed only in side or rear yards, cannot sit over easements or setbacks, and are capped at 15 feet tall. Call the Building Inspection Division at 512-218-5550 about older projects on your house. For fence permit questions, call Code Enforcement at 512-341-3329.

sections.h2: Do you need a certificate of occupancy?
sections.html:
For a house sale it usually means nothing. The city issues one only when a space is newly built, remodeled or renovated, and a new occupant who makes only cosmetic changes will not receive one.

  • The Fire Marshal's Office conducts annual fire safety inspections for commercial space, so this applies to a business, not a home sale.
  • If you converted a garage or finished an addition, ask the building office whether the permit was closed out.
  • For a move, contact Atmos for gas, Oncor for electricity and the city's utility billing office for water, and plan the transfers around your closing date.

The Williamson County and Cities Health District reviews food service plans, which would matter if you ran a home-based food business that you want to hand off with the house.

You may be able to, but check the city's current short-term rental and hotel occupancy tax rules first. Ordinances change, so ask the city before you list a short-term rental.

A tenant in place also complicates showings, and many buyers want the house empty at closing.

sections.h2: Homeowner exemptions and tax caps in Williamson County
sections.html:
Williamson Central Appraisal District sets home values, and a homeowner's exemption takes part of that value off the taxable total. A late application can be filed up to two years after the tax becomes delinquent, under Tax Code Section 11.431(a).

Round Rock homeowner exemption rules at Williamson CAD
TopicRule
Regular filing periodJanuary 1 through April 30
Late filingUp to two years after the tax becomes delinquent
ReapplyingNot needed unless the chief appraiser asks or you move
Buying after January 1Exemption can apply for part of the year if the previous owner had none
Cost to fileNothing; WCAD charges no fee

The age 65 exemption starts the year you turn 65, and a disability exemption generally tracks Social Security disability benefits. A mobile home owner must furnish the title or a verified purchase contract. A surviving spouse who is 55 or older can inherit a school tax ceiling, but only when the late spouse received the over-65 exemption.

sections.h2: Property tax deadlines at a Round Rock closing
sections.html: Round Rock follows the statewide tax calendar. At closing the title company settles whatever is owed for the year, along with any penalty. Request a current statement from the Williamson County tax office first. A bill still open on February 1 is delinquent and begins to build penalty and interest.

sections.h2: Inherited, in foreclosure or tied up with a tenant
sections.html:
Inheritance, foreclosure and tenancy each carry their own paperwork.

  • Inherited house: the deed route depends on whether a will exists, whether the owner recorded a beneficiary deed, or whether a court must appoint someone.
  • Foreclosure: a lender's sale is preceded by default and sale notices, so the calendar is fixed and a closing before the auction date matters.
  • Tenant: a written notice to vacate comes first, then a justice court case.

A title company can tell you what must be recorded before a buyer's lender will fund. The title company usually handles recording after closing, and the county clerk's fee schedule is in the Texas Courts clerk manual. Your settlement statement shows the final charge.

sections.h2: What happens between contract and closing
sections.html:
Once the contract is signed, the title company starts a file, runs the title search and requests your loan payoff. It also requests a tax statement from the Williamson County tax office. If an older permit was never closed out, the buyer's agent may raise it here, so call the Building Inspection Division early.

On closing day you sign the deed. Your loan and any tax due are paid out of the sale money, the deed is recorded, and the remainder is yours. A cash buyer needs no lender approval, so the closing date depends mostly on how quickly liens clear and the title work finishes.

Plan your move-out around the utilities. Atmos handles gas, Oncor handles electricity and the city's utility billing office handles water, and each needs a stop or transfer date that matches the day you hand over keys.

sections.h2: Weighing a cash offer against a listing
sections.html:
Cash buyers are busy in Round Rock, and what they offer reflects repairs and location. Take a listing estimate, remove commissions and carrying costs, and set the remainder beside the cash figure. Going cash avoids lender appraisal and repair haggling and lets you pick the date.

Before you decide, gather permit records, a tax statement and a payoff letter so each buyer sees the same facts and quotes you on the same basis.

faqs.q: Do cash buyers operate in Round Rock?
faqs.a: Yes. Offers vary with the condition and location of the house, so weigh a cash bid against a listing estimate after commissions and carrying costs.

faqs.q: Does a Round Rock fence repair require approval?
faqs.a: Call Code Enforcement at 512-341-3329, the number listed for fence permit questions. Building permits and inspections questions go to 512-218-5550.

faqs.q: Can I claim a homestead exemption after buying mid-year?
faqs.a: Possibly. A buyer who moves in after January 1 may qualify for the remaining months of that tax year if the prior owner held no homestead exemption.

faqs.q: When do Round Rock area property taxes become late?
faqs.a: Once January 31 passes. From February 1 an unpaid bill is delinquent and accrues penalty and interest.

faqs.q: Who pays to record the deed?
faqs.a: Usually the title company records it after closing, and the settlement statement lists the final charge.
